title: Size gevent's Hub threadpool to Locust's peak VU count
summary: MemoryStoreUser._run() already works around gevent/ibm_db's greenlet-boundary incompatibility, but the underlying gevent Hub threadpool defaults to 10 OS threads and is never resized — under BM-14a's 200 VUs the same 'Waiter.switch' assertion the fix targets still occurred 50 times in one run.
description:
`benchmarks/load/locustfile.py`'s `MemoryStoreUser._run()` (lines 224-251) is a documented, deliberate fix for a known gevent/`ibm_db` incompatibility: `ibm_db` is a blocking C extension gevent cannot monkeypatch, and naively calling it from a Locust `User` task (a greenlet) risks `AssertionError: Can only use Waiter.switch method from the Hub greenlet` when an exception crosses the OS-thread-to-greenlet boundary via gevent's internal `SimpleQueue`. The fix dispatches through `gevent.get_hub().threadpool.apply(...)` and catches/re-raises exceptions on the correct side specifically to avoid that assertion — see the docstring at lines 6-21 and 224-240 for the full explanation already written by whoever built this.

Despite that fix being in place and used by every task in the file (confirmed via `self._run(...)` call sites), the observed BM-14a run (200 VUs, 5 min, https://github.com/priyanshu-krishnan1/yaadien/actions/runs/31242532940/job/93077463451) still logged the exact same `Waiter.switch` `AssertionError` **50 times**, with tracebacks through `gevent/_gevent_cqueue.SimpleQueue._unlock` → `gevent/_gevent_c_waiter.Waiter.switch` — the precise path `_run()` was built to avoid.

gevent's `Hub` class defaults `threadpool_size` to 10 OS threads (`gevent.hub.Hub.threadpool_size`), and nothing in `locustfile.py` overrides it. BM-14a dispatches 200 concurrent VUs' worth of blocking `ibm_db` calls through that same 10-thread pool — a 20:1 oversubscription. Working hypothesis: under enough queueing pressure on the threadpool itself (not just on individual `fn` exceptions, which is what `_run()`'s wrapper handles), the same assertion class resurfaces via a different path inside gevent's threadpool/hub plumbing. This needs to be confirmed, not assumed — it's a hypothesis consistent with the evidence (the assertion appeared in the 200-VU step; grep the other jobs' logs for the same string at 50-VU scale to see if it's absent or just rarer there).

Investigate:
1. Confirm whether raising `gevent.get_hub().threadpool.maxsize` (e.g. to 200, or dynamically to the Locust `-u` value) before the run starts eliminates the residual assertions at 200 VUs.
2. If it does, add explicit threadpool sizing to `locustfile.py`'s `@events.init` handler (the same place `_STORE`/`_EMBED` are set up), sized to the run's peak VU count (Locust exposes this via `environment.parsed_options.num_users` in headless mode) or a generous fixed ceiling if that's simpler and safe.
3. If it doesn't fully eliminate the assertions, document the residual failure mode precisely (they may be genuinely harmless/cosmetic — confirm whether they correlate with any actual lost requests or just log noise) rather than leaving it as an open question.

Acceptance: re-run BM-14a (200 VUs) after the fix and confirm zero (or a documented, understood residual count of) `Waiter.switch` AssertionErrors in the job log; note the finding either way in this story's comments so CIF-2's failure-rate tuning isn't done against noisy data.
